questions.subject: LLMs
questions.question: Explain the difference between scaling laws and fine-tuning in LLMs.
questions.ideal_answer: scaling laws and fine-tuning differ in several ways: scaling laws is performance vs compute relationship (works by predictable improvement with scale) whereas fine-tuning is model adaptation technique (works by task-specific parameter update). scaling laws is typically used for loss ∝ C^-alpha, where C is compute, while fine-tuning is used for full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, prefix tuning. Example demonstrating scaling laws: Kaplan et al. 2020, Chinchilla optimal. Example demonstrating fine-tuning: LoRA: W = W_0 + BA, low-rank decomposition.
